name: Two Sicilies
bonus: grain, silk and the Strait of Messina pay the crown.
blurb: One king on both shores of the Strait of Messina: the realm on this side of the Lighthouse and the realm beyond it, joined at last.
history: Sicily and the south of Italy were one kingdom under the Normans; the Sicilian Vespers of 1282 split them into two crowns that both called themselves Sicily. Alfonso V of Aragon held both from 1442, and the name Two Sicilies became official in 1816.

name: Italy
bonus: the universities and workshops of the Renaissance serve one crown.
blurb: From the Alps to Sicily, the cities that taught Europe to paint, bank and build answer to one crown in Rome.
history: After Rome fell, Italy stayed divided among cities, princes, the Pope and foreign kings for more than thirteen centuries; Machiavelli ended The Prince with a plea for a redeemer to unite it. The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in 1861 and took Rome in 1870.

name: Roman Empire
bonus: Pax Romana, the old provinces accept the eagles again.
blurb: Rome and Constantinople under one throne again: the Empire of the Caesars, restored around its own sea.
history: The Roman Empire ruled the whole Mediterranean; its western half fell in 476, its eastern half lived on from Constantinople until 1453. Justinian won back Italy and Africa in the 500s; after 1453 Mehmed II took the title Caesar of Rome, and he landed troops at Otranto in 1480.

name: Spain
bonus: the tercios, pike and shot in great squares.
blurb: Castile and Aragon under one crown, Granada taken, and the whole of Spain turned outward to the sea.
history: Isabella of Castile and Ferdinand of Aragon married in 1469 and ruled their crowns together; Granada fell to them in 1492. Their grandson Charles reigned over both as King of Spain from 1516, under the red saltire of Burgundy.

name: Great Britain
bonus: an island that lives and fights at sea.
blurb: England and Scotland, so long at each other's throats, joined into one kingdom on one island.
history: James VI of Scotland became James I of England in 1603, ruling both crowns; the Acts of Union of 1707 made them one Kingdom of Great Britain, and its navy came to rule the seas.

name: Francia
bonus: counts and envoys of the crown bind new lands quickly.
blurb: The empire of Charlemagne whole again, from the Pyrenees to the Elbe, with Paris and Aachen in one hand.
history: Charlemagne ruled the Franks from Aachen and was crowned emperor in Rome in 800. His grandsons split the empire at Verdun in 843 into west, middle and east, the seeds of France, Lotharingia and Germany, and nobody has joined them since.

name: Netherlands
bonus: the counting houses and fleets of Amsterdam and Antwerp.
blurb: The seventeen provinces by the sea, their own masters, their ships in every harbour of the world.
history: The dukes of Burgundy gathered the Low Countries in the 1400s and held court in Brussels; under their Habsburg heirs the northern provinces rose against Spain in 1568 under the orange, white and blue of William of Orange.

name: Germany
bonus: the levies of a hundred principalities march under one banner.
blurb: The princes of the Empire under one crown at last, from the Rhine to the Oder, with its heart at Frankfurt on the Main.
history: The Holy Roman Empire was a patchwork of hundreds of princes, bishops and free cities. The Frankfurt Parliament of 1848 flew black, red and gold for a united Germany; Prussia made one in 1871.

name: Prussia
bonus: drill, discipline and an officer class that lives for war.
blurb: The sandy March of Brandenburg and the Order's Prussia joined under one black eagle.
history: In 1525 the last Grand Master of the Teutonic Order turned Lutheran and made Prussia a duchy for himself; it passed to his cousins of Brandenburg in 1618, and in 1701 the elector crowned himself King in Prussia.

name: Austria-Hungary
bonus: a crown of many crowns, held together by marriages and patience.
blurb: Vienna, Prague and Buda under one double-headed eagle: the great Danube monarchy.
history: Ladislaus the Posthumous wore the crowns of Austria, Bohemia and Hungary when he died in 1457. After Mohács in 1526 the Habsburgs inherited Bohemia and Hungary for good, and ruled the three together until 1918.

name: Scandinavia
bonus: free farmers who make stubborn soldiers.
blurb: The Kalmar Union made whole and lasting: Denmark, Norway and Sweden under one red cross on gold.
history: Queen Margaret united Denmark, Norway and Sweden at Kalmar in 1397 under a red cross on gold, but the Swedes broke away again and again until Gustav Vasa left for good in 1523.

name: Commonwealth
bonus: the winged hussars.
blurb: The Crown of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania as one Commonwealth of Two Nations, from the Baltic to the Dnieper.
history: Poland and Lithuania shared a king from 1386; the Union of Lublin in 1569 made them one Commonwealth with one parliament and an elected king, one of the largest states in Europe.

name: Russia
bonus: armies that know the winter and the long roads.
blurb: The scattered Rus principalities gathered into one Tsardom of All the Russias.
history: Ivan III of Moscow took Novgorod in 1478, threw off the Horde in 1480 and called himself sovereign of all Rus; his grandson Ivan IV was crowned Tsar in 1547.

name: Golden Horde
bonus: horse armies that strike before anyone can gather.
blurb: The heirs of Batu Khan reunited, the steppe one horde again and the Rus princes paying tribute once more.
history: The Golden Horde, the western part of the Mongol Empire, took tribute from the Rus for two centuries. By 1444 it had split into the Great Horde, Crimea, Kazan and others, and in 1502 the Crimeans sacked the last Great Horde capital.

name: Greece
bonus: the scholars of Mistra and the books of the Greeks.
blurb: The Greek lands free under a Greek crown, from the Morea to the islands. Byzantium may skip it and reach for Rome itself.
history: At Mistra in the Morea the philosopher Gemistos Plethon urged the emperors to rebuild a Greek state; the Morea fell in 1460. The Greeks rose in the Morea in 1821, and a Kingdom of Greece was recognised in 1832 under a white cross on blue.

name: Romania
bonus: Carpathian fortresses and forest strongholds.
blurb: Wallachia, Moldavia and Transylvania under one prince, the eagle and the aurochs side by side.
history: Michael the Brave of Wallachia held all three principalities in 1600, for a few months, before he was murdered; Wallachia and Moldavia united in 1859, and Transylvania joined them in 1918.

name: Serbian Empire
bonus: the mountain clans answer the tsar's call.
blurb: Dušan's empire of the Serbs and Greeks reborn, from the Danube to Thessaly.
history: Stefan Dušan was crowned Emperor of the Serbs and Greeks at Skopje in 1346 and ruled from the Danube to Thessaly; his empire broke apart soon after his death in 1355, and the Ottomans swallowed the pieces.

name: Sultanate of Rum
bonus: caravanserais on the roads from Konya to the sea.
blurb: Anatolia under the heirs of the Seljuks, ruled from Konya as in the days of the double-headed eagle.
history: The Seljuk Sultanate of Rum ruled Anatolia from Konya for two centuries after Manzikert in 1071 and built caravanserais along its roads. The Karamanids saw themselves as its heirs and fought the Ottomans for Anatolia until 1487.

name: Persia
bonus: the red-capped horsemen of the shah.
blurb: A Shah in Tabriz over the Turkmen confederations, and the old Persian crown worn again.
history: The Turkmen Black Sheep and White Sheep fought over Tabriz in the 1400s. In 1501 young Ismail, leading red-capped Qizilbash horsemen, took Tabriz and crowned himself Shah of Iran, founding the Safavid state.

name: Abbasid Caliphate
bonus: the wealth of the Nile and the Tigris in one treasury.
blurb: Mecca, Cairo, Damascus and Baghdad under one ruler, and the black banner of the Abbasids raised over them again.
history: The Abbasid caliphs ruled from Baghdad until the Mongols sacked it in 1258; the Mamluks of Cairo kept a shadow caliph and guarded Mecca, but never held Baghdad.

name: Maghreb
bonus: corsair galleys from every port of the coast.
blurb: The lands of the setting sun under one sultan, from the Atlantic to the Gulf of Sidra.
history: The Almohads ruled the whole Maghreb from Marrakesh in the 1100s; after them it split among Fez, Tlemcen and Tunis, and the Marinids of Fez tried and failed to put it back together in the 1340s.

name: Ghana
bonus: the gold and salt caravans across the Sahara.
blurb: The whole of the Sahel under one ruler, named for Wagadu, the first great empire of gold.
history: Ghana, or Wagadu, grew rich on the gold trade across the Sahara a thousand years ago. Mali followed it, then Songhai, which took Timbuktu in 1468; in 1957 the Gold Coast took the old empire's name.

name: Mexico
bonus: a populous land under one Huey Tlatoani.
blurb: The valley of Mexico and every people from the Gulf to the Pacific under the eagle of Tenochtitlan.
history: The Triple Alliance of Tenochtitlan, Texcoco and Tlacopan ruled central Mexico from 1428 and took tribute far to the south and east. Mexico took its name and its eagle from Tenochtitlan.

name: Kingdom of Jerusalem
bonus: crusaders who know why they came.
blurb: A Christian crown in Jerusalem once more, as in the days of the crusades.
history: The First Crusade founded the Kingdom of Jerusalem in 1099; Saladin took the city in 1187, and Acre fell in 1291. The Lusignan kings of Cyprus still called themselves kings of Jerusalem in 1444.

name: Kingdom of Burgundy
bonus: the richest towns north of the Alps pay one royal treasury.
blurb: The duchies and counties between France and the Empire joined into one kingdom, from the Zuiderzee to the Jura.
history: Charles the Bold took Lorraine in 1475 to join his northern and southern lands. He had already asked the Emperor for a royal crown at Trier in 1473, but Frederick III slipped away before the coronation, and Charles died at Nancy in 1477.

name: Greater Georgia
bonus: mountain fortresses in every pass of the Caucasus.
blurb: Georgia whole again and reaching to the Black Sea, as in the golden age of Queen Tamar.
history: Queen Tamar (1184-1213) ruled from the Black Sea to the Caspian, and in 1204 her armies helped her Komnenos kin found the Empire of Trebizond. Mongol invasions broke her kingdom apart, and by 1490 it had split into three.

name: Al-Andalus
bonus: the libraries of Córdoba open again.
blurb: The Reconquista turned back: the Nasrids of Granada rule Iberia as the caliphs of Córdoba once did.
history: The Umayyad caliphs of Córdoba ruled most of Iberia in the 900s. By 1444 only the Nasrid emirate of Granada was left of al-Andalus, and it fell to Castile and Aragon in 1492.

name: High Kingdom of Ireland
bonus: the clans answer one high king.
blurb: Dublin taken back from the English and the clans under one high king, as in the days of Brian Boru.
history: Brian Boru made himself High King of Ireland and died winning at Clontarf in 1014. By 1444 the English held only the Pale around Dublin; in 1642 the Confederate Irish flew a gold harp on green.
